title: "Packages"
description: |
  Find and install SEMinR for R, Python, and JavaScript/TypeScript.
toc: false
---

SEMinR is **R-first**: the [R package](https://github.com/sem-in-r/seminr) is the
authoritative implementation, and the Python and JavaScript/TypeScript ports
maintain **numerical parity** with it. It comes in **three variants** — pick the
one that fits your workflow:

::: {.variant-summary}
- <img src="images/logos/r.svg" alt="" class="lang-logo"> **R** — the authoritative package (on CRAN)
- <img src="images/logos/python.svg" alt="" class="lang-logo"> **Python** — a port on PyPI *(experimental)*
- <img src="images/logos/typescript.svg" alt="" class="lang-logo"> **JavaScript / TypeScript** — a port on npm *(experimental)*
:::

Each port is validated against R-generated fixtures on the bundled `mobi` / ECSI
dataset, and its public API mirrors SEMinR's familiar names.

> **Please note:** The Python and JavaScript/TypeScript ports are **experimental** for now.
> The R package remains the authoritative implementation; if you run into a problem
> with a port, please report it on that port's repository.

Select a tab below for installation instructions:

## <img src="images/logos/r.svg" alt="" class="lang-logo"> R

[[![SEMinR on CRAN](https://img.shields.io/cran/v/seminr.svg?label=CRAN&color=2166ac&style=flat-square)](https://cran.r-project.org/package=seminr)]{.pkg-badge}

The authoritative reference implementation. Estimates PLS-SEM (including
PLSc), covariance-based SEM, and CFA, with bootstrapping, PLSpredict, PLS-MGA,
interactions, and higher-order constructs.

**Install the released version from CRAN:**

```r
install.packages("seminr")
```

**Or install the development version from GitHub:**

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("sem-in-r/seminr")
```

Then load it:

```r
library(seminr)
```

- **Source:** <https://github.com/sem-in-r/seminr>
- **CRAN:** <https://cran.r-project.org/package=seminr>

## <img src="images/logos/python.svg" alt="" class="lang-logo"> Python

[[![SEMinR on PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/seminr.svg?label=PyPI&color=2166ac&style=flat-square)](https://pypi.org/project/seminr/)]{.pkg-badge}

A Python port with numerical parity to the R package (1e-5 for PLS quantities;
tiered tolerances for CBSEM). Requires Python 3.11+; runtime dependencies are
NumPy and SciPy only.

> **Experimental.** This port is still maturing — please report any issues on its
> [GitHub repository](https://github.com/sem-in-r/seminr-py/issues).

**Install from PyPI:**

```bash
pip install seminr
```

**Optional pandas support** (DataFrame input and `.to_dataframe()`):

```bash
pip install "seminr[pandas]"
```

- **Source:** <https://github.com/sem-in-r/seminr-py>
- **PyPI:** <https://pypi.org/project/seminr/>

## <img src="images/logos/typescript.svg" alt="" class="lang-logo"> JavaScript & TypeScript

[[![@seminr/core on npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@seminr/core.svg?label=npm&color=2166ac&style=flat-square)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@seminr/core)]{.pkg-badge}

A zero-dependency, runtime-agnostic (Bun, Node, Deno, browser) port for running
SEM analyses in a modern scripting runtime or embedding estimation in a product.
It installs and runs as plain JavaScript, and — being written in TypeScript —
ships first-class type declarations for TypeScript projects.

> **Experimental.** `seminr-ts` is in early development (`0.x`) — please report any
> issues on its [GitHub repository](https://github.com/sem-in-r/seminr-ts/issues).

**Install from npm:**

```bash
npm install @seminr/core
```

- **Source:** <https://github.com/sem-in-r/seminr-ts>
- **npm:** <https://www.npmjs.com/package/@seminr/core>

:::
